newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble steady on correction after Wednesday's fall.
newsitem.headline: Rouble steady on correction after Wednesday's fall.

text.p: The rouble was little changed on Thursday due to a short-term correction after banks had bought big dollar amounts from the central bank on Wednesday, dealers said.
"Banks bought many dollars yesterday from the central bank at its rates but they must be cutting their long positions as roubles are scarce now," one dealer said.
Dealers said the central bank dollar sales did not seem to be active intervention by the central bank. Commercial banks were simply buying from the central bank at its published rates.
Dealers said less money than forecast had returned to the currency market from yesterday's Treasury bill auctions, in which a total of 10.5 trillion roubles of paper was offered.
Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,368-71 per dollar. Dealers said they had risen earlier as high as 5,354 per dollar compared with 5,366-69 late on Wednesday.
Tomorrow roubles edged up to 5,363-65 per dollar from yesterday's late 5,368-69.
The central bank had kept 5,328/5,368 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Thursday.
Overnight rouble credits yielded 30-40 percent compared with Wednesday's late 5-15 percent.

"The central bank must have decided to stop the dollar's rise for a short term, while the general policy of the steady rouble fall in line with the corridor remains, " United Investment Bank chief dealer Alexander Suchkov said:
He added some speculative dollar selling could also be behind the rouble's current stability.
